value.value: 16,496 rising ninth-graders who applied to New York City Small Schools of Choice in the 2005–2006 through 2008–2009 admissions years; most SSC attendees were Black or Hispanic, and 83% qualified for free or reduced-price lunch.

Lottery-based instrumental-variable evaluation of enrollment in academically nonselective New York City Small Schools of Choice versus other city public high schools, with longitudinal secondary, postsecondary, and available state employment-record follow-up.
